questions.prompt: Inflammation triggered by complement differs from inflammation triggered by a cut in:

options.text: What causes mast cells to release histamine

questions.prompt: Which complement protein forms the ring-shaped pore in the membrane attack complex?
questions.explanation: C5b starts the assembly with C6–C8; C9 forms the ring.

questions.prompt: The membrane attack complex kills bacteria by:

options.text: Making pores that cause cell lysis

questions.prompt: Name the three outcomes of complement activation and what each accomplishes.
questions.explanation: Opsonization (C3b coats microbes to enhance phagocytosis), inflammation (C3a + C5a make mast cells release histamine), and the membrane attack complex (C5b–C9 punch pores that lyse the cell).
Interleukins are released by WBCs and influence other cells.

questions.prompt: Pyrogens cause fever by acting on the:
questions.explanation: They turn up the body's thermostat.

questions.prompt: Why can a low-grade fever help fight a bacterial infection?

options.text: Fever activates the membrane attack complex directly
Bacteria grow faster at higher temperatures, so they burn out
Bacterial enzymes fail faster than ours as temperature rises
Fever destroys viral RNA inside infected human cells

questions.explanation: A small temperature rise opens a gap between the two enzyme curves.

questions.prompt: Which statement about interferon is FALSE?

options.text: Interferon protects the cell that produced it.
Interferon can stimulate natural killer cells.
Interferon causes neighboring cells to make antiviral proteins.
Interferon is secreted by virus-infected cells.
Interferon is a nonspecific antiviral defense.

questions.explanation: The infected cell will likely die; interferon protects its neighbors.

questions.prompt: Antiviral proteins (AVPs) block viral infection by:
questions.explanation: They destroy viral mRNA so biosynthesis can't proceed.

questions.prompt: Why does injected interferon cause strong side effects?

options.text: It lowers body temperature below the healthy 37 °C set point
It causes allergic reactions by activating complement proteins
It spreads body-wide, so cells everywhere destroy their own RNA
It kills white blood cells along with the virus-infected cells

questions.prompt: Which molecule is found on the surface of many bacteria and can trigger complement nonspecifically?
Describe how interferon protects a neighboring cell from a virus, step by step.
questions.explanation: A virus infects a cell → the infected cell makes and secretes interferon → interferon binds receptors on neighboring cells → those cells make antiviral proteins → when a released virus enters and makes RNA, the AVPs destroy it, preventing infection.
